AARON ALDERMAN / sourcerer

An idea becomes a path.

Follow the work from an observation to an explanation, and from permission to a change someone can inspect.

← sourcerer / HomeThreadsMapQuestions

From a signal to a reason

An explanation should stay close to what can be observed and tested.

  1. What did the measurement miss?

    Two different things can look the same through one kind of measurement.

  2. Before you trust the reading, check the ruler.

    Before trusting a number, check what the tool can measure.

  3. Let the correction leave a seam.

    When an explanation changes, leave a way to understand why.

Permission before power

Follow the boundary between helping and taking authority.

  1. I can. May I? Should I?

    “Can I?”, “May I?” and “Should I?” are three different questions.

  2. An intention is not yet an action.

    Choosing to act and carrying out an action are different parts of a story.

  3. If you could control everything, should you?

    Being able to control something does not settle whether you should.

Leave a way to repair

Make memory and correction part of the ordinary route.

  1. Can someone else check the result?

    Keep enough of the method for someone else to check the result.

  2. Remember to care.

    Who or what needs my attention here?

  3. Let the correction leave a seam.

    When an explanation changes, leave a way to understand why.

The wider corpus remains open.
